meta.what: The HOOK LIBRARY. Every entry is a real hook that exists, quoted verbatim, with the numbers it earned. Nothing here was invented to sound plausible.
meta.operator: 2026-08-21 — 'the mold actually come from data and the swipe file for what we believe are high converting' / 'next to each mold I want the exact original hook variation'.
meta.twoKindsOfEvidence: swipeOriginal = a real thread from the swipe DB with its impressions. That proves REACH. ourBest = our own recreation with its Levanta CVR. That proves CONVERSION. A shape with only reach evidence is a bet; a shape with both is a template.
meta.whyThisReplacesTheOldMolds: The mold library promoted on revenue-per-1k-views, which rewards a thread for going viral. Three 'proven' molds (M1, M2, M3) are curiosity hooks that measured 0.00% CVR in the Levanta data despite huge reach. This library ranks on CVR, because the reader who clicks a shopping list already intends to buy and the reader who clicks a mystery does not.

fleetBaseline.note: 726 conversions over 20,462 clicks (300 subids); click and dollar rates per 1k views from the last 30 days of the registry, 2026-08-21

meta.correction: 2026-08-21, twice on the same shape. H7 was first published as 'never run' -- the operator supplied a live Magnus thread proving it had run five times. It was then republished as 'avoid' on a 1.68% CVR. The operator pushed back again, and re-measuring on earnings per view showed the shape is mid-table, not last. Both misses came from the same root: ranking a funnel on one of its two halves. Recorded rather than quietly edited, because the correction is more instructive than the entry.
meta.ranking: Ranked on DOLLARS PER 1,000 VIEWS, not CVR. The first version of this page ranked on CVR and got two shapes badly wrong in opposite directions: H5 showed the best CVR on the page (16.67%) while being the worst earner by 20x, because that rate sits on 54 clicks out of 9.3M views; H7 showed the worst CVR while out-earning it 47-fold, because it generates 9x the fleet click rate. CVR alone measures how well a click converts and says nothing about whether the thread produces clicks at all. All three numbers are kept -- clicks per 1k is the funnel's top, CVR is its bottom, dollars per 1k is the product of both.
meta.swipeDb: Swipe DB: base app7vXbBugWeCGctD, table tblS9wU39UjUVSsvl. Each shape's swipeOriginal carries airtableUrl, the card for the donor row, so the original can be opened where it was harvested rather than only on X.
meta.familyRule: A shape's swipe original and our version must be the SAME HOOK, at 90% Dice or better, or the pairing proves nothing: the donor's reach belongs to a hook we did not run. Operator rule, 2026-08-21. Enforcing it found four bad pairings in the first published version -- H4 at 15%, H7 at 13%, H5 at 0%, and H2/H6 paired to the wrong creator entirely despite identical hook TEXT (the same hook had been posted by several accounts). Two of those inflated the reach claim: H2 showed 2.4M where its real donor had 1.0M, H6 showed 1.7M against a real 1.0M. Donors are now resolved from the ledger's sourceUrl -- what the thread was actually built from -- not by matching hook text.
meta.siblings: alsoInSwipe holds hooks that LOOK like the same shape but are separate threads by separate creators. Operator, 2026-08-21: 'technically those one elements can be considered another format by itself'. Agreed — each is a candidate PARENT with zero children, not a footnote on this one. They are listed here with their own cards so a promotion is a copy, not a re-hunt. Promote one when we actually run it: it becomes a parent, the run becomes its first child, and it stops borrowing this shape's numbers.
meta.candidates: Hooks with real reach that we have NOT run. Each is a parent-in-waiting: promote it when we ship it, and that first run becomes its first child. They were previously listed inside the shapes as 'same shape in the swipe file'. Operator, 2026-08-21: 'These are like different structure completely.' Measured, and correct — not one scored above the 90% family bar against the shape it was filed under; the closest was 80% and most were under 20%. Grouping them by theme let them borrow numbers from shapes they have nothing structurally to do with, which is the same error as pairing a donor by hook text instead of provenance.

shapes.name: Stack reveal
shapes.why: The whole cabinet, so the plug budget is the highest of any shape. Enormous reach in the swipe file and it PULLS CLICKS HARD — 1,381 link clicks on 668k views. But the clicks do not convert: 1,723 affiliate clicks returned 29 sales, 1.68%, less than half the fleet baseline. The reader who opens a 40-item cabinet tour is browsing, not shopping, and five plugs give them five chances to keep browsing. High reach and high CTR on a low CVR is the most expensive kind of thread we run.

shapes.verdict: KEEP, and it is the click engine. Worst CVR in the library at 0.47x fleet, but it produces 2.58 affiliate clicks per 1k views -- 9x the fleet rate -- and nets $0.234 per 1k views, 5.3x fleet. A low conversion RATE on a huge click VOLUME still out-earns a high rate on no clicks. Judging this shape on CVR alone was the error; it is 5th of 7 on earnings, not last.
